Appendix A Compactness of Best-Fit on Power-of-Two Workloads

This appendix formalises Observation 1 of Section 4.1. We consider the restricted setting in which every multi-GPU instance has demand gi∈{2,4,8}g_{i}\in\{2,4,8\}, i.e. the active workload is contained in ℐFF\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{FF}}, and the cluster runs a stripped-down variant of Algorithm 1: each arrival is handled by a single 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾\mathsf{Place} call that uses best-fit (no 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} pass on arrival), and each departure is handled by per-instance 𝖱𝖾𝗆𝗈𝗏𝖾\mathsf{Remove} calls followed by a single 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} pass on the departure side only. We show that this minimal policy is already sufficient to enforce SIFπ​(t)≤2/N\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t)\leq 2/N at all times, and we exhibit a finite event sequence that reaches the bound.

A.1. Setup and statement

Let the active workload consist of items of size g∈{2,4,8}g\in\{2,4,8\} that arrive and depart online, and let each node be a bin of capacity G=8G=8. We use Φπ​(t):=ν⁡(Pπ​(t))\Phi^{\pi}(t):=\nu(P^{\pi}(t)) for the partial-node count under policy π\pi at time tt, with Fπ​(t)=Φπ​(t)/NF^{\pi}(t)=\Phi^{\pi}(t)/N as in Section 3.2. The free space of a partial bin lies in {2,4,6}\{2,4,6\}, because used capacity attainable by sums of items in {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\} that strictly under-fill G=8G=8 is one of {2,4,6}\{2,4,6\}.

Proposition 0 (Best-Fit Compactness on Power-of-Two Workloads).

Let the policy place every arriving instance via best-fit, i.e. on the node leaving the smallest remaining capacity after placement and opening a fresh node when no existing node can host the instance, and let every departure be followed by a single 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} pass. If every active instance has gi∈{2,4,8}g_{i}\in\{2,4,8\}, then for every t≥0t\geq 0 the state σ⁡(t)\sigma(t) produced by the policy satisfies

Φπ​(t)≤ 2andSIFπ​(t)≤2N,\Phi^{\pi}(t)\;\leq\;2\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t)\;\leq\;\frac{2}{N},

and both inequalities are tight in the sense that a finite arrival sequence reaches Φπ​(t)=2\Phi^{\pi}(t)=2.

A.2. Proof of Proposition 1

We bound Φπ​(t)\Phi^{\pi}(t) separately on the two event types and combine the bounds. Throughout, “bin” is interchangeable with “node” and “item” with “instance”.

Part 1: best-fit on arrival leaves at most two partial bins.

We first show that immediately after any arrival event the cluster state has at most two partial bins.

Lemma B.1 (free-value uniqueness).

At any time during the arrival pass, at most one partial bin has remaining free space rr for each r∈{2,4,6}r\in\{2,4,6\}.

Proof.

Suppose for contradiction that two partial bins AA and BB have free space rr at the same time. Let BB be the bin whose free space last became rr, and consider the placement event that produced free⁡(B)=r\mathrm{free}(B)=r. Just before that placement, free⁡(A)=r\mathrm{free}(A)=r already held by hypothesis. The placement put an item of size ss into BB, with s≤free​(B)befores\leq\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}} and free​(B)before−s=r\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}-s=r, so free​(B)before≥s\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}\geq s. If BB was a fresh bin, then free​(B)before=G=8\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}=G=8 and s=G−r>0s=G-r>0; bin AA also had free space r≥sr\geq s, since r=G−sr=G-s and G≥sG\geq s forces r≥0r\geq 0, and we ruled out r=0r=0 because AA is partial. Concretely, for every reachable r∈{2,4,6}r\in\{2,4,6\} the item size s=G−r∈{6,4,2}s=G-r\in\{6,4,2\}, but only s∈{2,4}s\in\{2,4\} are admissible power-of-two items (size 66 is not in the workload), so the only case is s∈{2,4}s\in\{2,4\}, in which AA with free⁡(A)=r\mathrm{free}(A)=r also has free⁡(A)≥s\mathrm{free}(A)\geq s and best-fit would have picked AA over the fresh BB because the fresh bin has G=8>rG=8>r. If BB was not fresh, then free​(B)before>r\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}>r, so free⁡(A)=r<free​(B)before\mathrm{free}(A)=r<\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}. Best-fit’s least-fit rule would then still have preferred AA over BB, because AA leaves the smaller free space, provided AA can host the item. The admissibility condition free⁡(A)≥s\mathrm{free}(A)\geq s is exactly r≥sr\geq s. It holds because the placement into BB required free​(B)before≥s\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}\geq s, and substituting r=free​(B)before−sr=\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}-s rewrites r≥sr\geq s as free​(B)before≥2​s\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}\geq 2s. The only case where free⁡(A)<s\mathrm{free}(A)<s is when r<sr<s, but this is already excluded by the construction free​(B)before=r+s\mathrm{free}(B)_{\mathrm{before}}=r+s and the item size ss being one of {2,4}\{2,4\} which gives r+s≤Gr+s\leq G hence r≤G−sr\leq G-s. In every admissible sub-case best-fit’s tie-breaking prefers AA, contradicting the placement having gone to BB. ∎

Lemma B.2 (free-six isolation).

If some partial bin has free space 66, then no other partial bin exists at the same time.

Proof.

A bin with free=6\mathrm{free}=6 contains exactly one size-22 item. Consider the most recent placement that put this size-22 item into the bin. The bin was empty just before the placement, because no other item-size combination from {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\} yields used capacity 22. Best-fit opens a fresh empty bin only when no existing partial bin admits the item. The arriving item has size 22, so an admissible partial bin would only require free≥2\mathrm{free}\geq 2, which every partial bin satisfies because every partial free value lies in {2,4,6}\{2,4,6\}. Hence no partial bin existed at the moment the size-22 item was placed in the fresh bin, and the new free=6\mathrm{free}=6 bin is the sole partial bin at that instant.

Each subsequent arrival event either (i) places a size-22 item, which best-fit routes into the existing free=6\mathrm{free}=6 bin and reduces its free space to 44, removing it from the free=6\mathrm{free}=6 class; or (ii) places a size-44 item, which best-fit routes into the existing free=6\mathrm{free}=6 bin and reduces its free space to 22; or (iii) places a size-88 item, which opens a fresh bin that immediately becomes full and creates no new partial bin. In none of these cases is a second partial bin created while the original free=6\mathrm{free}=6 bin still has free space 66, so the isolation invariant is preserved until the next departure event. ∎

Lemma B.3 (two-partial bound).

At any time immediately after an arrival placement, the cluster has at most two partial bins, and the only reachable two-partial configuration has free spaces {2,4}\{2,4\}.

Proof.

Combining Lemmas B.1 and B.2, the set of free-space values present across partial bins is a subset of {2,4,6}\{2,4,6\} in which each value appears at most once, and the value 66 cannot coexist with any other partial bin. Hence the only feasible multisets of free-space values across partial bins are ∅\emptyset, {2}\{2\}, {4}\{4\}, {6}\{6\}, {2,4}\{2,4\}, {2,6}\{2,6\}, {4,6}\{4,6\} from cardinality counting, and the last two are forbidden by Lemma B.2. The remaining configurations have at most two partial bins. ∎

Part 2: Compact on departure leaves at most one partial bin.

Departures invoke a single 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} pass after the per-instance 𝖱𝖾𝗆𝗈𝗏𝖾\mathsf{Remove} calls have been applied. Under the present restriction ℐ=1=∅\mathcal{I}^{=1}=\emptyset, ℐFUF=∅\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{FUF}}=\emptyset, so the active 1-GPU population n1​(t)n_{1}(t) is identically zero and the total slot vacancy aggregated across anchored fragmentation-unfriendly instances is identically zero. The Workload Composition Condition (9) therefore reduces to 0≥00\geq 0 and holds trivially at every time. Lemma A.3 of Appendix B then contributes zero non-fully-packed pool nodes because no pool nodes exist, and Lemma A.4 of Appendix B contributes at most one non-fully-packed slotted node from the width-44 and width-22 𝖡𝖾𝗌𝗍𝖥𝗂𝗍𝖣𝗋𝖺𝗂𝗇\mathsf{BestFitDrain} passes. The post-departure state therefore satisfies Φπ​(t)≤1\Phi^{\pi}(t)\leq 1.

Combining the two parts.

The cluster state changes only at event boundaries. After every arrival event Part 1 gives Φπ​(t)≤2\Phi^{\pi}(t)\leq 2, and after every departure event Part 2 gives Φπ​(t)≤1≤2\Phi^{\pi}(t)\leq 1\leq 2. The bound Φπ​(t)≤2\Phi^{\pi}(t)\leq 2 therefore holds at every event boundary and extends to every continuous time instant between consecutive events, so

Φπ​(t)≤ 2,\displaystyle\Phi^{\pi}(t)\;\leq\;2,
Fπ​(t)=Φπ​(t)N≤2N,\displaystyle F^{\pi}(t)\;=\;\frac{\Phi^{\pi}(t)}{N}\;\leq\;\frac{2}{N},
SIFπ​(t)≤Fπ​(t)≤2N.\displaystyle\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t)\;\leq\;F^{\pi}(t)\;\leq\;\frac{2}{N}.

for all t≥0t\geq 0, where the last inequality uses the non-negativity of the inherent fragmentation F⋆​(t)F^{\star}(t) from Section 3.2.

Tightness.

The bound Φπ​(t)=2\Phi^{\pi}(t)=2 is realised by the following arrival sequence on an otherwise fully-packed cluster. Suppose all nodes other than one are fully packed and the remaining node hosts a single size-44 anchor together with one size-22 anchor, leaving free space 22. A DLT job composed of three size-44 instances now arrives. Best-fit considers each arriving instance in turn. The first instance encounters free space 22 on the partial node, which does not admit a size-44 item, so a fresh node is opened and the first instance is placed there, producing a new partial node with free space 44. The second instance sees free space 22 on the original partial node and free space 44 on the just-opened node, prefers the smaller fitting capacity, and is placed onto the just-opened node, which becomes fully packed. The third instance again finds the original partial node uninhabitable for a size-44 item and the now-full node also unable to host it, so a further fresh node is opened with free space 44. The cluster now contains two partial nodes, one with free space 22 and one with free space 44, matching the only feasible two-partial configuration identified in Lemma B.3 and witnessing Φπ​(t)=2\Phi^{\pi}(t)=2 together with SIFπ​(t)=2/N\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t)=2/N. This completes the proof of Proposition 1. ∎

Appendix B Proofs for the Theoretical Guarantees of COMPASS-ABS

This appendix collects the detailed proofs of the three results stated in Section 4.4, namely the unconditional state-space invariance in Proposition 6, the conditional SIF≤2/N\mathrm{SIF}\leq 2/N compactness bound in Theorem 7, and the per-operator complexity in Proposition 8. We keep the notation introduced in Section 4.2 for the ABS domain Σ\Sigma and in Section 4.3 for the three operators 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾\mathsf{Place}, 𝖱𝖾𝗆𝗈𝗏𝖾\mathsf{Remove}, and 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact}.

B.1. Proof of Proposition 6 (State-Space Invariance)

We prove that every event applied by Algorithm 1 maps Σ\Sigma into Σ\Sigma, so that by induction every state generated from an initial σ0∈Σ\sigma_{0}\in\Sigma remains in Σ\Sigma. Since the algorithm decomposes each job-level event into a finite sequence of per-instance operator calls together with at most one 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} call, it suffices to show that each operator branch preserves Σ\Sigma when applied to a state already in Σ\Sigma.

Place preserves Σ\Sigma.

Consider an arrival ii with demand gig_{i} applied to σ∈Σ\sigma\in\Sigma. We argue on the branches of 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾\mathsf{Place}.

If gi≥2g_{i}\geq 2, the operator selects a width w=w⋆​(gi)∈{2,4,8}w=w^{\star}(g_{i})\in\{2,4,8\} and a host n⋆n^{\star} such that either n⋆n^{\star} is already slotted with G−∑s∈S⁡(n⋆)w⁡(s)≥wG-\sum_{s\in S(n^{\star})}w(s)\geq w, or n⋆n^{\star} was empty and is promoted to slotted with an empty profile. In the first case, appending a slot of width ww to S⁡(n⋆)S(n^{\star}) produces a new slot multiset whose total width is at most GG and whose constituents lie in {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\}, hence the new S⁡(n⋆)S(n^{\star}) remains in 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿\mathsf{SlotConf} as defined in (5). In the second case, the post-event S⁡(n⋆)={w}S(n^{\star})=\{w\} trivially lies in 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿\mathsf{SlotConf}. The anchor of the new slot is set to ii so that w⁡(s⋆)=w⋆​(gi)=w⋆​(ga⁡(s⋆))w(s^{\star})=w^{\star}(g_{i})=w^{\star}(g_{a(s^{\star})}), which matches the constraint of Definition 2. The associated filler set is initialised to the up-to-rr migrated 1-GPU instances with r=w−gir=w-g_{i}, so that |F⁡(s⋆)|≤r=w⁡(s⋆)−ga⁡(s⋆)|F(s^{\star})|\leq r=w(s^{\star})-g_{a(s^{\star})} and the capacity invariant (4) holds as an inequality. Every pool node from which a filler is drawn loses one occupant and therefore preserves |P⁡(n)|≤G|P(n)|\leq G. No other node is touched.

If gi=1g_{i}=1, the operator places ii either into a slot vacancy (ga⁡(s)+|F⁡(s)|<w⁡(s))(g_{a(s)}+|F(s)|<w(s)), or into a non-full pool node (|P⁡(n)|<G)(|P(n)|<G), or onto a freshly promoted pool node initialised with P⁡(n)={i}P(n)=\{i\}. In the first case, |F⁡(s)||F(s)| increases by one and the new value remains bounded by w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)w(s)-g_{a(s)} by the entry condition ga⁡(s)+|F⁡(s)|<w⁡(s)g_{a(s)}+|F(s)|<w(s). In the second case, |P⁡(n)||P(n)| increases by one and remains bounded by GG. In the third case, the new pool node has |P⁡(n0)|=1≤G|P(n_{0})|=1\leq G. In all three cases the affected node remains a legal pool node or slotted node, and no slot configuration leaves 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿\mathsf{SlotConf}.

Remove preserves Σ\Sigma.

Consider a departure ii applied to σ∈Σ\sigma\in\Sigma.

If ii is an anchor of some slot ss, the operator dissolves ss and reinserts each filler f∈F⁡(s)f\in F(s) by the 1-GPU rule of 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾\mathsf{Place}. Dissolving ss removes one element from S⁡(n)S(n) for the host node nn, so the new S⁡(n)S(n) is a sub-multiset of the original S⁡(n)∈𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿S(n)\in\mathsf{SlotConf}, and any sub-multiset of a 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿\mathsf{SlotConf} element again lies in 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿\mathsf{SlotConf}. The reinsertion step has already been shown to preserve Σ\Sigma in the Place argument above, applied instance-by-instance to the elements of F⁡(s)F(s).

If ii is a 1-GPU instance currently attached as a filler in some slot ss, the operator simply removes ii from F⁡(s)F(s), which can only decrease |F⁡(s)||F(s)| and therefore preserves (4) as a strict inequality. If ii is a 1-GPU pool occupant on some pool node nn, the operator removes ii from P⁡(n)P(n), which only decreases |P⁡(n)||P(n)| and remains bounded by GG.

Compact preserves Σ\Sigma.

Migrations (x,ndst)(x,n_{\mathrm{dst}}) executed within the 𝖡𝖾𝗌𝗍𝖥𝗂𝗍𝖣𝗋𝖺𝗂𝗇\mathsf{BestFitDrain} loop are performed only when room𝒞​(ndst)≥size⁡(x)\mathrm{room}_{\mathcal{C}}(n_{\mathrm{dst}})\geq\mathrm{size}(x) holds for the current class 𝒞\mathcal{C}. Concretely, for the pool pass the destination pool node has |P⁡(ndst)|<G|P(n_{\mathrm{dst}})|<G before the migration, so |P⁡(ndst)||P(n_{\mathrm{dst}})| stays at most GG after the migration. For the width-44 pass the destination slotted node has ⌊D⁡(ndst)/4⌋≥1\lfloor D(n_{\mathrm{dst}})/4\rfloor\geq 1 so that D⁡(ndst)≥4D(n_{\mathrm{dst}})\geq 4, hence appending a width-44 slot keeps ∑s∈S⁡(ndst)w⁡(s)+4≤G\sum_{s\in S(n_{\mathrm{dst}})}w(s)+4\leq G and the new S⁡(ndst)S(n_{\mathrm{dst}}) remains in 𝖲𝗅𝗈𝗍𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖿\mathsf{SlotConf}. The width-22 pass is analogous with the inequality D⁡(ndst)≥2D(n_{\mathrm{dst}})\geq 2. Migrating a slot also detaches its filler set and reattaches it to the new host, which by the capacity invariant ga⁡(s)+|F⁡(s)|≤w⁡(s)g_{a(s)}+|F(s)|\leq w(s) on the source side remains valid on the destination side because w⁡(s)w(s) does not change under migration. Every migration therefore preserves Σ\Sigma, and so does the entire 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} call which is a finite composition of such migrations.

Conclusion.

By induction on the event sequence, every state produced by Algorithm 1 remains in Σ\Sigma, which establishes Proposition 6. ∎

B.2. Proof of Theorem 7 (Compactness under the Workload Composition Condition)

Throughout this subsection we assume that the fraction-form Workload Composition Condition (9) stated inside Theorem 7 holds at the time tt under consideration. The argument proceeds in three stages. We first translate the fraction form into a structurally more convenient slot-vacancy form (Lemma A.1), then show that this slot-vacancy form implies the saturation of every anchored fragmentation-unfriendly slot at the end of each operator call (Lemma A.2), and finally show that the three 𝖡𝖾𝗌𝗍𝖥𝗂𝗍𝖣𝗋𝖺𝗂𝗇\mathsf{BestFitDrain} passes inside 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} leave at most one partial node per node-type (Lemmas A.3 and A.4), which after normalisation by the cluster size NN yields the SIFπ​(t)≤2/N\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t)\leq 2/N bound.

Lemma A.1 (Slot-Vacancy Form of the Workload Composition Condition)

The fraction-form condition (9) is algebraically equivalent to the slot-vacancy form

(18) n1(t)≥∑s:a⁡(s)≠∅(w(s)−ga⁡(s)),n_{1}(t)\;\geq\;\sum_{s:\,a(s)\neq\varnothing}\bigl(w(s)-g_{a(s)}\bigr),

which asserts that the active 1-GPU population is at least as large as the total slot vacancy currently exposed by anchored fragmentation-unfriendly instances.

Proof.

By Definition 1, every active anchor a⁡(s)∈ℐ≥2a(s)\in\mathcal{I}^{\geq 2} has a slot width w⁡(s)=w⋆​(ga⁡(s))w(s)=w^{\star}(g_{a(s)}). Inspecting w⋆w^{\star} in (3) we obtain w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)=0w(s)-g_{a(s)}=0 for ga⁡(s)∈{2,4,8}g_{a(s)}\in\{2,4,8\}, w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)=1w(s)-g_{a(s)}=1 for ga⁡(s)=3g_{a(s)}=3, w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)=3w(s)-g_{a(s)}=3 for ga⁡(s)=5g_{a(s)}=5, w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)=2w(s)-g_{a(s)}=2 for ga⁡(s)=6g_{a(s)}=6, and w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)=1w(s)-g_{a(s)}=1 for ga⁡(s)=7g_{a(s)}=7. Summing over all active anchors and grouping by demand,

∑s:a⁡(s)≠∅(w(s)−ga⁡(s))=n3(t)+3n5(t)+2n6(t)+n7(t).\sum_{s:\,a(s)\neq\varnothing}\bigl(w(s)-g_{a(s)}\bigr)\;=\;n_{3}(t)+3\,n_{5}(t)+2\,n_{6}(t)+n_{7}(t).

Substituting this identity into (18) and dividing both sides by ntotal​(t)>0n_{\mathrm{total}}(t)>0 yields (9), and the implication is reversible since each step is an equivalence. In what follows we use (18) interchangeably with the original form. ∎

Lemma A.2 (Slot Saturation under the Workload Composition Condition)

Under (18), at the end of every event handled by Algorithm 1 (whether a job arrival or a job departure) the capacity invariant in (4) holds with equality for every active fragmentation-unfriendly anchor, namely

(19) ga⁡(s)+|F⁡(s)|=w⁡(s)∀s​ with ​a​(s)∈ℐFUF.g_{a(s)}+|F(s)|\;=\;w(s)\qquad\forall s\text{ with }a(s)\in\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{FUF}}.
Proof.

By construction 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾\mathsf{Place} pulls w⁡(s)−ga⁡(s)w(s)-g_{a(s)} fillers from the pool whenever a fragmentation-unfriendly anchor is installed, and 𝖱𝖾𝗆𝗈𝗏𝖾\mathsf{Remove} in the 1-GPU branch additionally migrates one replacement filler from the pool whenever a filler departs from a slot. Both operators therefore actively maintain the saturation equality (19) as long as the pool population is non-empty. The only obstacle is filler shortage at the moment when fillers are being drawn, and the slot-vacancy form (18) guarantees that the total active 1-GPU population n1​(t)n_{1}(t) is at least the total slot vacancy aggregated across all anchored fragmentation-unfriendly instances at the end of the event. Since 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} does not create new slot vacancy and the 1-GPU pool is internally redistributed across pool nodes without changing n1​(t)n_{1}(t), (18) carries through to the post-𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} state. Because Algorithm 1 now invokes 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} at the end of both arrival and departure branches, every event terminates in a post-𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} state, and the equality (19) therefore holds at the end of every event. ∎

Lemma A.3 (Pool Pass Compactness)

After the pool pass of 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact}, at most one pool node is non-fully-packed.

Proof.

The pool pass instantiates 𝖡𝖾𝗌𝗍𝖥𝗂𝗍𝖣𝗋𝖺𝗂𝗇\mathsf{BestFitDrain} policy with countpool​(n)=|P⁡(n)|\mathrm{count}_{\mathrm{pool}}(n)=|P(n)|, cappool​(n)=G\mathrm{cap}_{\mathrm{pool}}(n)=G, and roompool​(n)=G−|P⁡(n)|\mathrm{room}_{\mathrm{pool}}(n)=G-|P(n)|, and the set of partial hosts is 𝒩={n:0<|P⁡(n)|<G}\mathcal{N}=\{n:0<|P(n)|<G\}. Each iteration picks the head of 𝒩\mathcal{N} as nsrcn_{\mathrm{src}}, the node with the largest remaining room. The drain loop selects, for each 1-GPU item xx on nsrcn_{\mathrm{src}}, the eligible destination with the smallest room roompool​(ndst)≥1\mathrm{room}_{\mathrm{pool}}(n_{\mathrm{dst}})\geq 1 and migrates xx there. Each migration strictly increases |P⁡(ndst)||P(n_{\mathrm{dst}})| and strictly decreases |P⁡(nsrc)||P(n_{\mathrm{src}})|.

The loop terminates either when |𝒩|≤1|\mathcal{N}|\leq 1 or when no progress is made during an iteration. Suppose for contradiction that termination occurs with |𝒩|≥2|\mathcal{N}|\geq 2 and no progress in the last iteration. “No progress” means that for every xx on nsrcn_{\mathrm{src}} the eligible set 𝒮={n∈𝒩∖{nsrc}:roompool​(n)≥1}\mathcal{S}=\{n\in\mathcal{N}\setminus\{n_{\mathrm{src}}\}:\mathrm{room}_{\mathrm{pool}}(n)\geq 1\} is empty. But |𝒩|≥2|\mathcal{N}|\geq 2 implies the existence of at least one n′∈𝒩∖{nsrc}n^{\prime}\in\mathcal{N}\setminus\{n_{\mathrm{src}}\} with |P⁡(n′)|<G|P(n^{\prime})|<G, equivalently roompool​(n′)≥1\mathrm{room}_{\mathrm{pool}}(n^{\prime})\geq 1, so n′∈𝒮n^{\prime}\in\mathcal{S}, a contradiction. Therefore termination implies |𝒩|≤1|\mathcal{N}|\leq 1, which is exactly the claim that at most one pool node is non-fully-packed. ∎

Lemma A.4 (Slotted Compactness)

After the width-44 and width-22 passes of 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact}, and under the slot saturation guaranteed by Lemma A.2, at most one slotted node is non-fully-packed.

Proof.

Under Lemma A.2 every active slot is internally saturated, so a slotted node nn is non-fully-packed if and only if D⁡(n)=G−∑s∈S⁡(n)w⁡(s)>0D(n)=G-\sum_{s\in S(n)}w(s)>0, i.e. the node has unprofiled residual capacity. Possible values of ∑s∈S⁡(n)w⁡(s)\sum_{s\in S(n)}w(s) are subsums of multisets drawn from {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\} bounded above by G=8G=8, so a fully-packed slotted node has ∑s∈S⁡(n)w⁡(s)=8\sum_{s\in S(n)}w(s)=8 achieved by one of the multisets {8}\{8\}, {4,4}\{4,4\}, {4,2,2}\{4,2,2\}, {2,2,2,2}\{2,2,2,2\}, while a non-fully-packed slotted node has ∑s∈S⁡(n)w⁡(s)≤6\sum_{s\in S(n)}w(s)\leq 6 achieved by one of {2}\{2\}, {4}\{4\}, {2,2}\{2,2\}, {4,2}\{4,2\}, {2,2,2}\{2,2,2\}.

The width-44 pass treats anchored width-44 slots as items and slotted nodes as hosts, with countw4​(n)\mathrm{count}_{\mathrm{w4}}(n) counting width-44 anchored slots in S⁡(n)S(n) and roomw4​(n)=⌊D⁡(n)/4⌋\mathrm{room}_{\mathrm{w4}}(n)=\lfloor D(n)/4\rfloor. Repeating the contradiction argument of Lemma A.3 with the width-44 class, if the width-44 pass terminates with two or more nodes still satisfying 0<countw4​(n)<capw4​(n)0<\mathrm{count}_{\mathrm{w4}}(n)<\mathrm{cap}_{\mathrm{w4}}(n) and with positive room on at least one of them, then the head source has an eligible destination and the loop must perform a migration, contradicting the no-progress termination condition. The pass therefore terminates with at most one slotted node in the width-44 partial set.

After the width-44 pass, consider the remaining partial slotted nodes. Each such node either has no width-44 slot at all, or it is the unique node left in the width-44 partial set. The first sub-population is then processed by the width-22 pass under the same argument applied to the width-22 class. The same no-progress contradiction shows that the width-22 pass terminates with at most one node in the width-22 partial set.

It remains to argue that the survivor of the width-44 pass and the survivor of the width-22 pass can be taken to be the same node. Suppose the width-44 pass leaves a single partial node n(4)n^{(4)} and the width-22 pass leaves a single partial node n(2)≠n(4)n^{(2)}\neq n^{(4)}. The node n(4)n^{(4)} contains a single width-44 anchored slot and has D⁡(n(4))∈{0,2}D(n^{(4)})\in\{0,2\} from the multiset enumeration above. If D⁡(n(4))=0D(n^{(4)})=0 then n(4)n^{(4)} is fully-packed, contradicting its membership in the partial set; therefore D⁡(n(4))=2D(n^{(4)})=2, which means S⁡(n(4))={4}S(n^{(4)})=\{4\}, because {4,2}\{4,2\} already exhausts the width-22 room and {4,4}\{4,4\} is fully-packed. But then roomw2​(n(4))=⌊2/2⌋=1≥1\mathrm{room}_{\mathrm{w2}}(n^{(4)})=\lfloor 2/2\rfloor=1\geq 1, so n(4)n^{(4)} is a width-22-eligible destination that can absorb any width-22 slot present on n(2)n^{(2)}. The width-22 pass would therefore have made a migration from n(2)n^{(2)} to n(4)n^{(4)}, contradicting the assumption that the width-22 pass left n(2)≠n(4)n^{(2)}\neq n^{(4)}. We conclude that the survivor sets of the two passes coincide, hence at most one slotted node remains partial after the entire 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} call. ∎

Concluding the proof of Theorem 7

Combining Lemmas A.3 and A.4, immediately after every 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} invocation performed by Algorithm 1 under the Workload Composition Condition (9), at most one pool node and at most one slotted node are non-fully-packed, so at most two non-empty nodes in the cluster carry unused GPU capacity. Because Algorithm 1 invokes 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} in both the arrival branch and the departure branch, every event handled by the algorithm terminates in a state that satisfies this two-partial-node bound. The cluster state changes only at event boundaries, so the bound extends from every event boundary to every continuous time instant between consecutive events; that is, the two-partial-node bound holds for all t≥0t\geq 0.

It remains to translate this combinatorial bound into the Scheduler-Induced Fragmentation metric of Section 3. Recall that Fπ​(t)F^{\pi}(t) denotes the proportion of partial nodes in the cluster state produced by policy π\pi, that F⋆​(t)≥0F^{\star}(t)\geq 0 denotes the inherent partial-node proportion attainable by any feasible packing of the active demand ℐ⁡(t)\mathcal{I}(t), and that SIFπ​(t):=Fπ​(t)−F⋆​(t)\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t):=F^{\pi}(t)-F^{\star}(t). Dividing the partial-node count by the cluster size NN converts the two-partial-node bound into Fπ​(t)≤2/NF^{\pi}(t)\leq 2/N for all t≥0t\geq 0, and the non-negativity of F⋆​(t)F^{\star}(t) then gives

SIFπ​(t)=Fπ​(t)−F⋆​(t)≤Fπ​(t)≤2N∀t≥0.\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t)\;=\;F^{\pi}(t)-F^{\star}(t)\;\leq\;F^{\pi}(t)\;\leq\;\frac{2}{N}\qquad\forall\,t\geq 0.

This completes the proof of Theorem 7. ∎

B.3. Proof of Proposition 8 (Operational Complexity)

We bound the per-operator running time under the standard assumption that the slot index, the pool index, and the empty-node index are maintained as balanced search trees keyed by the relevant priority. The bookkeeping cost of incremental index maintenance is absorbed into the operator-level bounds below.

Place is O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N).

The multi-GPU branch performs three operations on the slotted-node index: a candidate query for the smallest remaining capacity above the threshold w⋆​(gi)w^{\star}(g_{i}), an insertion of a new slot record, and at most w⋆​(gi)−gi≤6w^{\star}(g_{i})-g_{i}\leq 6 filler-draw operations from the pool index. Each of these operations runs in O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N) on a balanced search tree of NN entries, and the constant number of filler draws contributes only an O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N) overhead. The 1-GPU branch performs one priority query for an open slot vacancy or a non-full pool node, again at O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N) cost. Therefore 𝒯⁡(𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾)=O⁡(log⁡N)\mathcal{T}(\mathsf{Place})=O(\log N).

Remove is O⁡(1)O(1).

If ii is a 1-GPU occupant, the operator detaches ii from its current container in O⁡(1)O(1) time by following the parent pointer maintained in the slot or pool index. If ii is an anchor of slot ss, the operator dissolves ss in O⁡(1)O(1) time and reinserts each of the |F⁡(s)|≤6|F(s)|\leq 6 fillers by the 1-GPU rule of 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾\mathsf{Place}, each at O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N) cost. Since |F⁡(s)||F(s)| is bounded by the constant G−ga⁡(s)≤6G-g_{a(s)}\leq 6, the total work of an anchor departure is dominated by a constant number of O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N) filler reinsertions, so the local handler cost is O⁡(1)O(1) when the filler reinsertions are charged to the subsequent 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} pass that already runs in O⁡(N)O(N). We therefore report 𝒯⁡(𝖱𝖾𝗆𝗈𝗏𝖾)=O⁡(1)\mathcal{T}(\mathsf{Remove})=O(1) for the local edit.

Compact is O⁡(N)O(N).

A single pass of 𝖡𝖾𝗌𝗍𝖥𝗂𝗍𝖣𝗋𝖺𝗂𝗇\mathsf{BestFitDrain} visits each partial host at most once as nsrcn_{\mathrm{src}} in the outer loop, and inside the loop it performs at most count𝒞​(nsrc)≤G\mathrm{count}_{\mathcal{C}}(n_{\mathrm{src}})\leq G item migrations, each at O⁡(log⁡N)O(\log N) cost. The total work per class is therefore O⁡(N​log⁡N)O(N\log N), and aggregating across the three classes (pool, w4, w2) gives the same asymptotic bound. With a slightly tighter amortised analysis that charges each migration to the destination node whose room strictly decreases as a result, the log⁡N\log N factor collapses to O⁡(N)O(N) total, matching the bound stated in the proposition. ∎

Appendix C Algorithm for Computing Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t) and F⋆​(t)F^{\star}(t)

The inherent fragmentation defined in Section 3.2 is

F⋆​(t)=Φ⋆​(t)N,Φ⋆​(t):=minP​ feasible⁡ν⁡(P),F^{\star}(t)\;=\;\frac{\Phi^{\star}(t)}{N},\qquad\Phi^{\star}(t)\;:=\;\min_{P\text{ feasible}}\nu(P),

where ν⁡(P)\nu(P) is the number of partial nodes in a feasible packing PP of the instantaneous instance multiset ℐ⁡(t)\mathcal{I}(t) and Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t) is the minimum partial-node count attainable across all such packings. Throughout this appendix the algorithm computes the integer-valued Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t), from which F⋆​(t)F^{\star}(t) follows by the single division by the cluster size NN. Evaluating Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t) via a general bin-packing solver is already expensive on a single time slice and prohibitive on a trace-long evaluation. The structural analysis carried out in Section 4 for COMPASS-ABS, however, supplies enough structure to compute Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t) either in closed form or by a small residual ILP. We describe the algorithm in this appendix and then use it as the oracle scheduler SIFOpt in the empirical evaluation of Section 5.

C.1. Key observation: reduing to power-of-two items

Each fragmentation-unfriendly instance g∈ℐFUFg\in\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{FUF}} can be combined with strictly smaller active instances into a composite block whose total GPU count falls in {4,8}\{4,8\}, namely

g=3:\displaystyle g=3:\quad 3+1=4,\displaystyle 3+1=4,
g=5:\displaystyle g=5:\quad 5+3=8​or​ 5+2+1=8​or​ 5+1+1+1=8,\displaystyle 5+3=8\;\text{or}\;5+2+1=8\;\text{or}\;5+1+1+1=8,
g=6:\displaystyle g=6:\quad 6+2=8​or​ 6+1+1=8,\displaystyle 6+2=8\;\text{or}\;6+1+1=8,
g=7:\displaystyle g=7:\quad 7+1=8.\displaystyle 7+1=8.

If every active FUF instance is paired into such a composite, the remaining item population consists of composites of size {4,8}\{4,8\}, original ℐFF\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{FF}} instances of size {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\}, and any 1-GPU instances not consumed as fillers, so the multiset of item sizes is contained in {1,2,4,8}\{1,2,4,8\}. The Workload Composition Condition (9) stated in Theorem 7 is exactly the algebraic condition under which the active 1-GPU population is sufficient to complete this pairing for every FUF instance, so under that condition the reduction to a power-of-two item multiset always succeeds.

C.2. Closed form solution under the Workload Composition Condition

When all item sizes lie in {1,2,4,8}\{1,2,4,8\}, packing into bins with capacity G=8G=8 admits an trivial optimum: a Best-Fit-Decreasing pass that processes items in the order 8→4→2→18\to 4\to 2\to 1 always closes one bin per multiple of GG and leaves at most one partial bin whose load equals T⁡(t)modGT(t)\bmod G, where

(20) T⁡(t):=∑g=18g⋅ng​(t)T(t)\;:=\;\sum_{g=1}^{8}g\cdot n_{g}(t)

denotes the total active GPU demand at time tt. This is because every two width-4 items pack into a single full bin, every four width-2 items pack into a single full bin, every eight width-1 items pack into a single full bin, and any residual mixture below capacity GG collapses into a single tail bin by the nested-power-of-two structure. The number of partial bins in the optimal packing is therefore

(21) Φ⋆(t)= 1[T(t)≢0(modG)]={0,T⁡(t)modG=0,1,otherwise,\Phi^{\star}(t)\;=\;\mathbb{1}\bigl[T(t)\not\equiv 0\pmod{G}\bigr]\;=\;\begin{cases}0,&T(t)\bmod G=0,\\ 1,&\text{otherwise,}\end{cases}

F⋆​(t)=Φ⋆​(t)/N∈{0, 1/N}F^{\star}(t)=\Phi^{\star}(t)/N\in\{0,\,1/N\}. In other words, under the condition the inherent fragmentation floor never exceeds a single node: at most one bin carries unavoidable residue T⁡(t)modGT(t)\bmod G, and every partial node beyond that one is therefore scheduler-induced and accounted for by SIFπ​(t)\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}(t). Both cases of (21) are tight and achievable by the explicit Best-Fit-Decreasing placement described below.

C.3. Residual ILP when the Workload Composition Condition fails

When (9) fails, the active 1-GPU population is short by δ⁡(t):=(n3+3​n5+2​n6+n7)−n1\delta(t):=\bigl(n_{3}+3n_{5}+2n_{6}+n_{7}\bigr)-n_{1} relative to the filler demand of the FUF anchors. After the greedy combining stage exhausts the 1-GPU supply, exactly δ⁡(t)\delta(t) units of FUF slot vacancy remain unfilled, equivalently a small residual subset U⁡(t)⊆ℐFUFU(t)\subseteq\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{FUF}} of FUF instances enter the placement stage still carrying their original size in {3,5,6,7}\{3,5,6,7\}. The item multiset is therefore no longer contained in {1,2,4,8}\{1,2,4,8\}, and the closed form (21) no longer applies.

In that case we restrict the optimization to U⁡(t)U(t): we first place all power-of-two items via Best-Fit-Decreasing as in the closed-form case, then run an integer linear program that places the residual FUF instances on top of the resulting state and minimises the total partial-node count. The size of this ILP is governed by |U⁡(t)||U(t)| rather than ntotal​(t)n_{\mathrm{total}}(t), and |U⁡(t)||U(t)| is in turn bounded by δ⁡(t)\delta(t), which is empirically a small constant on production traces because the Workload Composition Condition holds during the overwhelming majority of evaluated time slices and fails only briefly during transient mixture shifts.

C.4. Algorithm summary

We now state the procedure explicitly. The inputs are the active instance counts n1​(t),…,n8​(t)n_{1}(t),\ldots,n_{8}(t) at time tt; the outputs are the optimal partial-node count Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t) and a witness packing P⋆​(t)P^{\star}(t) realising it (which the SIFOpt oracle scheduler uses as its target placement). The normalised inherent fragmentation F⋆​(t)F^{\star}(t) used in Section 3.2 is then obtained as F⋆​(t)=Φ⋆​(t)/NF^{\star}(t)=\Phi^{\star}(t)/N.

Logic of the procedure.

The algorithm proceeds in two stages that mirror the structural analysis of Section 4. The combining stage (lines 3–6) absorbs every fragmentation-unfriendly instance into a composite block of size {4,8}\{4,8\} by pairing it with strictly smaller active instances. Combining priorities are chosen so as to consume the smallest number of 1-GPU instances first when the fragmentation-unfriendly size already has a natural partner of non-unit size in the active set (e.g., 5+35+3 before 5+1+1+15+1+1+1); the priority order does not affect Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t) as long as combining succeeds for all FUF instances, because the resulting power-of-two item multiset has the same total T⁡(t)T(t) and Best-Fit-Decreasing on a power-of-two item set always attains the bin-count lower bound ⌈T⁡(t)/G⌉\lceil T(t)/G\rceil. The placement stage (line 7) then runs Best-Fit-Decreasing in the order 8→4→2→18\to 4\to 2\to 1 and materialises this lower bound. Under the Workload Composition Condition, the closed form (21) reads off the partial-node count directly from T⁡(t)modGT(t)\bmod G without ever inspecting the placement, but the placement is still produced as a witness so that the SIFOpt oracle scheduler has a concrete target to migrate towards in its evaluation runs. When the condition fails, the residual ILP at lines 12–13 handles the small subset of FUF instances that the combining stage could not pair, and the size of that ILP is bounded by the deficit δ⁡(t)=(n3+3​n5+2​n6+n7)−n1\delta(t)=(n_{3}+3n_{5}+2n_{6}+n_{7})-n_{1} rather than by the cluster size, so the procedure remains tractable on production traces even when (9) is momentarily violated.

Complexity.

The combining stage scans the instance multiset once at O​(ntotal​(t))O(n_{\mathrm{total}}(t)) cost. The Best-Fit-Decreasing placement runs in O⁡(ntotal​(t)​log⁡ntotal​(t))O(n_{\mathrm{total}}(t)\log n_{\mathrm{total}}(t)) with a balanced search tree keyed by bin remaining capacity, and degenerates to O​(ntotal​(t))O(n_{\mathrm{total}}(t)) for the power-of-two item set because each item closes exactly one bin position. Whenever (9) holds, the closed-form return at line 8 short-circuits the placement step for the purpose of reporting Φ⋆​(t)\Phi^{\star}(t), so the dominant cost is the linear-time combining and the optional witness materialisation. When (9) fails, the residual ILP at line 12 runs on at most δ⁡(t)≤|U⁡(t)|\delta(t)\leq|U(t)| variables and remains millisecond-scale on production traces with δ⁡(t)\delta(t) of the order of tens.

Appendix D Extension to Multi-Panel NVLink Communication Domains

The COMPASS-ABS design developed in Section 4 hardwires the per-node GPU count at G=8G=8 together with the slot widths {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\}, both of which trace back to the DGX-1 / HGX baseboard abstraction in which a single node forms one NVLink communication domain. Recent NVIDIA platforms such as NVL72 and the projected NVL576 extend the high-bandwidth NVLink fabric across multiple baseboards inside a single rack-scale assembly, so that the basic intra-instance communication domain now contains GdomG_{\mathrm{dom}} GPUs with GdomG_{\mathrm{dom}} no longer equal to 88. Throughout this appendix we assume only that

(22) Gdom=Gp⋅K,Gp= 8,K∈ℤ≥1,G_{\mathrm{dom}}\;=\;G_{p}\cdot K,\qquad G_{p}\;=\;8,\qquad K\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1},

namely that each NVLink communication domain comprises exactly KK baseboards of Gp=8G_{p}=8 GPUs each. The original DGX-1 / HGX system corresponds to K=1K=1, NVL72 corresponds to K=9K=9, and a hypothetical NVL576 corresponds to K=72K=72 if treated as a single flat domain or K=8K=8 if treated as eight NVL72 sub-domains. The structural fact we exploit is that the 88-GPU baseboard survives across all of these platforms as the basic hardware building block; only the number of baseboards that sit inside a single NVLink domain varies.

We refer to a Gp=8G_{p}=8 baseboard as a panel throughout this appendix. Workloads on a multi-panel NVLink domain now admit two qualitatively different instance classes:

  • •

    Sub-panel instances with gi∈{1,…,8}g_{i}\in\{1,\ldots,8\} that fit within one panel, exactly as in the original setting; and

  • •

    Multi-panel instances with gi∈{16,24,32,40,48,56,64,…,Gdom}g_{i}\in\{16,24,32,40,48,56,\allowbreak 64,\ldots,G_{\mathrm{dom}}\} that span multiple panels in the same NVLink domain through the rack-scale NVLink fabric.

The within-panel intra-instance constraint of Section 2.2 is replaced by an intra-domain constraint: every GPU assigned to a single instance must lie in the same NVLink domain. Sub-panel instances satisfy this trivially; multi-panel instances exercise it.

D.1. Hierarchical Anchor-Based Space

We extend COMPASS-ABS to a two-level scheduler that runs the original within-panel policy on each panel and a structurally identical panel-level analogue across panels within each NVLink domain. The panel-level state space Σpanel\Sigma_{\mathrm{panel}} mirrors the ABS construction of Section 4.2 verbatim under two substitutions: the panel replaces the GPU as the atomic placement unit, and the domain capacity KK replaces the node capacity G=8G=8. A multi-panel instance of demand gig_{i} has panel demand pi:=gi/Gp∈{2,3,…}p_{i}:=g_{i}/G_{p}\in\{2,3,\ldots\} and is anchored in a panel-slot of width wp⋆​(pi)∈{2,4,8}w_{p}^{\star}(p_{i})\in\{2,4,8\} panels:

(23) wp⋆​(p)={2,p=2,4,p∈{3,4},8,p∈{5,6,7,8}.w_{p}^{\star}(p)\;=\;\begin{cases}2,&p=2,\\ 4,&p\in\{3,4\},\\ 8,&p\in\{5,6,7,8\}.\end{cases}

Multi-panel instances with pi∈{2,4,8}p_{i}\in\{2,4,8\} are called panel-fragmentation-friendly (panel-FF); those with pi∈{3,5,6,7}p_{i}\in\{3,5,6,7\} are panel-fragmentation-unfriendly (panel-FUF). A 1-panel instance, namely a gi=Gp=8g_{i}=G_{p}=8 instance that fully occupies one baseboard, plays at the panel level the role that a 1-GPU instance plays at the GPU level inside a panel: it can either saturate a panel-vacancy in an anchored panel-FUF panel-slot, or sit in a panel-pool reserved for panel-level fillers. The full cluster-wide state space is the Cartesian product across NVLink domains of Σpanel\Sigma_{\mathrm{panel}}, with the internal state of each non-saturated panel still drawn from the GPU-level Σ\Sigma of Section 4.2. We call the resulting two-level state space the hierarchical ABS and denote it by Σhier\Sigma_{\mathrm{hier}}.

D.2. Hierarchical Workload Composition Condition

The Workload Composition Condition (9) of Theorem 7 extends to the two-level setting by imposing one condition per level. Let ng​(t)n_{g}(t) denote the count of active sub-panel instances of GPU demand g∈{1,…,8}g\in\{1,\ldots,8\} at time tt, and let np(panel)​(t)n_{p}^{(\mathrm{panel})}(t) denote the count of active multi-panel instances of panel demand p∈{2,3,…}p\in\{2,3,\ldots\}. The GPU-level condition stays identical to (9), namely

(24) n1​(t)≥n3​(t)+3​n5​(t)+2​n6​(t)+n7​(t),n_{1}(t)\;\geq\;n_{3}(t)+3n_{5}(t)+2n_{6}(t)+n_{7}(t),

and the panel-level condition takes the structurally identical form

(25) n8​(t)≥n3(panel)​(t)+3​n5(panel)​(t)+2​n6(panel)​(t)+n7(panel)​(t),n_{8}(t)\;\geq\;n_{3}^{(\mathrm{panel})}(t)+3n_{5}^{(\mathrm{panel})}(t)+2n_{6}^{(\mathrm{panel})}(t)+n_{7}^{(\mathrm{panel})}(t),

where the left-hand side is the active count of gi=8g_{i}=8 instances, treated as 1-panel fillers at the panel level. Equation (25) is obtained from (24) by the substitution 1​-GPU↦1​-panel1\text{-GPU}\mapsto 1\text{-panel} together with the analogue of the slot-vacancy form (18) at panel granularity, and uses the same coefficient pattern {1,3,2,1}\{1,3,2,1\} for the same algebraic reason as in Lemma A.1.

D.3. Hierarchical COMPASS algorithm

The extended scheduler adopts two structurally identical 𝖯𝗅𝖺𝖼𝖾/𝖱𝖾𝗆𝗈𝗏𝖾/𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Place}/\mathsf{Remove}/\mathsf{Compact} pipelines, one per level, dispatched according to the demand class of the arriving or departing instance:

  • •

    Sub-panel events (gi≤8g_{i}\leq 8): handled by the GPU-level COMPASS-ABS of Section 4.3 acting on the host panel.

  • •

    Multi-panel events (gi∈{16,24,…,Gdom−Gp}g_{i}\in\{16,24,\ldots,G_{\mathrm{dom}}-G_{p}\}): handled by the panel-level analogue acting on the host NVLink domain, with gi=8g_{i}=8 instances serving as panel-fillers.

  • •

    Domain-filling events (gi=Gdomg_{i}=G_{\mathrm{dom}}): occupy an entire NVLink domain at once and are treated as a width-KK degenerate panel-slot.

Algorithm 1 is invoked at both levels and each 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍\mathsf{Compact} pass runs over the BestFitDrain classes for its level. At the GPU level the three classes remain {pool,w4,w2}\{\mathrm{pool},\mathrm{w}_{4},\mathrm{w}_{2}\} on capacity Gp=8G_{p}=8; at the panel level they become {panel​-​pool,panel​-​w4,panel​-​w2}\{\mathrm{panel\text{-}pool},\allowbreak\mathrm{panel\text{-}w_{4}},\mathrm{panel\text{-}w_{2}}\} on capacity KK. Because the two levels act on disjoint populations of items, the two compaction passes do not interfere and run independently after each event.

D.4. Hierarchical compactness guarantee

The compactness guarantee of Theorem 7 lifts to the hierarchical setting in a structurally identical form.

Theorem 1 (Hierarchical Compactness).

Assume that the GPU-level Workload Composition Condition (24) and the panel-level Workload Composition Condition (25) both hold at every t≥0t\geq 0. Then in every cluster state produced by the hierarchical COMPASS-ABS scheduler:

  1. (1)

    across the entire cluster, at most one panel-resident slotted GPU-region and at most one panel-resident GPU-pool region are non-fully-packed; and

  2. (2)

    within each NVLink domain that hosts at least one multi-panel anchor, at most one panel-slot region and at most one panel-pool region are non-fully-packed.

Consequently, after normalising the partial-region count at each level by the corresponding domain size, the GPU-level and panel-level scheduler-induced fragmentation measures satisfy

(26) SIFGPUπ​(t)≤2Np(cluster-wide, Np panels),\displaystyle\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}_{\mathrm{GPU}}(t)\;\leq\;\frac{2}{N_{\mathrm{p}}}\quad\text{(cluster-wide, $N_{\mathrm{p}}$ panels)},
SIFpanelπ​(t)≤2K(per NVLink domain of K panels),\displaystyle\mathrm{SIF}^{\pi}_{\mathrm{panel}}(t)\;\leq\;\frac{2}{K}\quad\text{(per NVLink domain of $K$ panels)},

for all t≥0t\geq 0.

Proof sketch.

The argument reduces to two independent invocations of the proof of Theorem 7 given in Appendix B.2, one on the GPU-level state inside each panel and one on the panel-level state inside each NVLink domain. Both invocations are valid because Lemmas A.1–A.4 of Appendix B.2 depend only on (i) the power-of-two slot widths {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\} being a valid sub-decomposition of the local capacity, (ii) the anchor-filler invariant under the friendly/unfriendly dichotomy of (23), and (iii) the class structure {pool,w4,w2}\{\text{pool},\text{w}_{4},\text{w}_{2}\} on which 𝖡𝖾𝗌𝗍𝖥𝗂𝗍𝖣𝗋𝖺𝗂𝗇\mathsf{BestFitDrain} operates, all of which are preserved under the substitution G→KG\to K and 1​-GPU→1​-panel1\text{-GPU}\to 1\text{-panel} at the panel level. ∎

D.5. Generality with respect to the domain panel count

Theorem 1 is stated for an arbitrary positive integer KK, without assuming that KK is a power of two. The panel-level BestFitDrain operates on class set {panel​-​pool,panel​-​w4,panel​-​w2}\{\mathrm{panel\text{-}pool},\allowbreak\mathrm{panel\text{-}w_{4}},\allowbreak\mathrm{panel\text{-}w_{2}}\} exactly as the GPU-level pass operates on its own class set, and the combinatorial argument of Lemma A.4 does not depend on GG taking any particular value beyond requiring that the slot widths {2,4,8}\{2,4,8\} remain a valid sub-decomposition of the capacity. For the NVL72 instantiation with K=9K=9, any panel-level layout decomposes into at most one width-88 panel-slot together with one residual panel acting as a panel-pool, which is the structural reason the 99-panel layout fits cleanly into the existing framework despite K=9K=9 not being a power of two: the lone residual panel coincides exactly with the panel-pool slot that the framework already requires. The same hierarchical scheduler and the same compactness bound apply to every multi-panel platform whose NVLink domain comprises an integer number of 88-GPU baseboards, including the original DGX-1 / HGX system (K=1K=1, in which the panel level is trivially empty), DGX-2 and SuperPod intermediate systems (K=2K=2), the NVL72 system (K=9K=9), and the projected NVL576 system (K=72K=72 flat, or K=8K=8 across NVL72 sub-domains as a third tier). In summary, as long as the NVLink domain contains an integer multiple of Gp=8G_{p}=8 GPUs, the hierarchical COMPASS-ABS scheduler remains valid and the SIF bound (26) continues to hold.
